problem_found: Wikipedia gives opening figures as free text in inconsistent forms (day vs weekend, worldwide vs India, ranges, USD)
action_taken: Saved all 38 candidate sentences; one verified phrase per film chosen in data/manual/first_weekend_phrases.csv
why: No single regex picks the right figure on every page; a human choice that the script verifies word-for-word against the source is transparent and cannot invent numbers

problem_found: Infobox has no Budget field for some films
action_taken: Kept films; budget left missing (NULL) for them
why: Budget is a confounder we describe, not our outcome — dropping films for it would shrink an already small n

problem_found: YouTube comment JSON contains author names, channel ids and profile URLs
action_taken: Dropped 5 identifying columns during flattening: authorDisplayName, authorProfileImageUrl, authorChannelUrl, authorChannelId, channelId
why: Brief's ground rule: protect people. Usernames never leave data/raw/, which is gitignored

problem_found: Channel search returned promo videos (launch events, speeches, Shorts, 30 s cut-downs) whose titles contain 'trailer'
action_taken: Kept only the main trailer plus videos with 'trailer' in the title, no promo words, and length within 10% of the main trailer
why: Dubbed language versions are the same edit, so same length; counting promos would inflate views for films with busy channels (Peddi had 16 'trailer' videos, 1 real)

problem_found: TMDb genres and cast are lists inside JSON, which do not fit in one table cell
action_taken: Joined genre names into one comma-separated text column; kept only top-3 billed cast
why: One row per film keeps the films table simple; we describe genre/cast, we don't model them

problem_found: Same film spelled differently across 5 sources (e.g. TMDb 'Kantara - A Legend: Chapter 1', YouTube 'RAID 2 (TRAILER): Ajay D | ...')
action_taken: Normalised titles (lowercase, removed brackets, 'trailer', language tags, text after '|', punctuation) then rapidfuzz-scored against the 10 canonical titles
why: A shared film_id is what lets us JOIN trailers, box office, comments and trends

action_taken: 70–94: sent to a human (M9, data/manual/match_review.csv); below 70: rejected
why: A wrong join silently corrupts every later number, so uncertain matches are checked by a person

problem_found: Yearly grossing table row 'Dhurandhar' (the 2025 prequel) looks like 'Dhurandhar: The Revenge'
action_taken: Rejected by token_sort_ratio (extra words lower the score), not joined to any film
why: partial_ratio would have scored it 100 and joined the wrong film's ₹1,350 crore gross
